asian_option_pricer.text: `compound_option_pricer` prices an option on another option (call or put on a call or put) using the exact Geske (1979) closed form, so it answers "what is the premium-bearing right to buy or sell an option worth?" It takes two strikes (`strike_underlying` and `strike_compound`) and two expiries (`tau_compound` and `tau_underlying`). `asian_option_pricer` answers a different question: what is an option on the average price of the underlying worth? It uses Monte Carlo with `n_steps` averaging observations and `n_simulations` paths. Averaging lowers volatility, so an Asian option is worth less than the corresponding vanilla European option. Practically, the compound pricer is deterministic and ignores `n_simulations` and `seed`, while the Asian pricer's estimate depends on them. Both can return Greeks via the `greeks` flag.

explain.text: `compound_option_pricer` (Compound Option Pricer) prices an option on another option, using the Geske (1979) closed-form formula. It covers all four standard types: call-on-call, call-on-put, put-on-call and put-on-put, chosen with `compound_type`. You supply the spot, the underlying option's strike (`strike_underlying`), the premium-style strike of the compound (`strike_compound`), the rate, `sigma`, and the two expiries (`tau_compound`, `tau_underlying`). Setting `greeks` to true also returns delta, gamma, vega, theta and rho, calculated by bumping inputs and repricing. The price is exact rather than simulated, so `n_simulations` and `seed` are kept only for older call signatures.

when.text:
Use the Compound Option Pricer (`compound_option_pricer`) when you need the price of an option whose underlying is itself an option:

- You want a call or put on a call or put. It supports all four types via `compound_type` (`call-on-call`, `call-on-put`, `put-on-call`, `put-on-put`).
- You want an exact closed-form price (Geske 1979) rather than a simulation. `n_simulations` and `seed` are retained only for backward-compatible calls and don't affect the price.
- You have two expiries: `tau_compound` for the compound option and a longer `tau_underlying` for the underlying option, plus separate strikes (`strike_compound` is the premium paid, `strike_underlying` is the underlying option's strike).
- You also want delta, gamma, vega, theta and rho from the same price. Set `greeks` to true, and they are computed by bump-and-reprice.
